question: Out-of-process adapter hop (postcard frames over UDS/pipe) same-core vs cross-core on a 1-vCPU-class host: p50/p99 round trip and calls/s/core, 64 B and 64 KiB

measured.label: N95 1-core stand-in, not a KVM VPS; grade <=B
measured.hardware: kamrui: Intel N95 (4 Gracemont cores, shared 2 MiB L2, no SMT), bare metal, kernel 6.17.0-41-generic, governor powersave, clock ~2.1 GHz same-core / 0.9-1.55 GHz cross-core runs; steal 0; loadavg 0.54 at start (Forgejo idle)
measured.conditions: port of research/state/raw/round-003/02-bench UDS+postcard path (+ pipe pair); client core 3, server core 3 (same) or 2 (cross) via sched_setaffinity; blocking, 1 call in flight, echo handler; 5 reps ABBA; n=20000 (64 B) / 3000 (64 KiB); bands = min-max (median)
measured.contended_rerun: CBMC neighbour on the server core, loadavg ~6: UDS 64 B p50 19.2 us same / 18.2 us cross (budget ~5.2-5.5k)
measured.laptop_contrast: i9-14900HX, contended, provisional: UDS 64 B p50 4.9 us same (reproduces round-3 4.8), 4.9 us cross (round-3 8.07); N95 hop ~2.9x laptop

decision_effect: R-MOD-1 (ARCHITECTURE s3.8 adapter isolation) budget text changes from 'Hop 4.8 us same core / 8.07 us cross core; budget rate x 8.07 us <=10% of a core ~ 12.4k calls/s/core (laptop, re-baseline on T1)' to 'Hop 14.2 us same core / 15.3 us cross core on the N95 1-core stand-in (B, not a KVM VPS); budget rate x hop <=10% of a core ~ 6.5k calls/s/core at household tier (laptop 4.9 us -> ~20k); re-baseline on a real KVM'. BENCH_PLAN W6 '~12.4k calls/s/core at 8.07 us' and ARCHITECTURE s6 IPC-hop row / small-node 'adapter hop budget ~12.4k' follow. Option for the spec author (not decided here): a pipe-pair transport measured 7.6 / 11.2 us (13.1k / 8.9k calls/s/core) on the same box.
rung: measurement grade B (single LAN stand-in host, bare-metal N95); not a T1 KVM result
reproduce: cd spikes/q3-002 && CARGO_TARGET_DIR=$PWD/target ../../ci/heavy.sh cargo build --release --offline && ssh kamrui 'mkdir -p ~/aegis-spike-q3/q3-002' && scp target/release/ipchop bench.sh kamrui:aegis-spike-q3/q3-002/ && ssh kamrui 'cd ~/aegis-spike-q3/q3-002 && ./bench.sh ./ipchop kamrui-ipc.jsonl 3 2 5' && scp kamrui:aegis-spike-q3/q3-002/kamrui-ipc.jsonl . && python3 -I summarize.py kamrui-ipc.jsonl
limits: Not a KVM guest (no virtualised IPIs/timers, which usually make cross-core wake-ups costlier; no steal; no SMT sibling). N95 under powersave at 0.9-2.1 GHz is likely slower than a typical $5 vCPU, so a real VPS could land under 12 us and revert this flip. Echo handler only, one call in flight (no batching); shm/futex, TCP and fd-passed bodies not re-measured; server CPU/call includes exec + warm-up. Laptop contrast contended.
